# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Housing, Mortgage & KiwiSaver Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset maintained by HLF (Home Loan Factory, https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/). Last verified: 10 November 2026 (2026-11-10T00:19:20Z).

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Reference Records (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/

## Canonical Statistic Reference Pages
- [Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs investors (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): Because mortgage applications often combine two incomes, approved first-home buyers in September 2026 recorded an average gross borrower income of $144.2k nationwide.
- [Annual residential construction cost inflation (CPI purchase of newly built home) (September 2026 quarter)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/): Residential build-cost inflation has settled into single digits compared with the post-pandemic construction surge—Stats NZ recorded a +3.2% annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home in the September 2026 quarter, alongside 3.7% overall CPI inflation.
- [First-home buyer high-DTI (>6x) lending share & bank speed-limit headroom (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/dti-headroom/): Most first-home lending currently sits well inside the Reserve Bank's Debt-to-Income limits—in September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer lending had a DTI ratio above 6x, sitting 10.9 percentage points below RBNZ's 20% bank speed-limit allowance.
- [Total monthly dollar equity unlocked via mortgage top-ups (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/equity-topup-demand/): Tapping into home equity without selling is one of the most common moves in New Zealand banking—in September 2026, homeowners unlocked $962m in mortgage top-ups across 9,639 existing properties (averaging $100k per top-up) for renovations, debt consolidation, and investment deposits.
- [First-home buyers approved with a 20% or greater deposit (<=80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-20-deposit-club/): Crossing the 20% deposit mark unlocks sharp advertised bank special rates and avoids low-equity margins. In September 2026, 1,325 first-home buyers (49.7% of approvals, or $680m) bought with a 20%+ deposit, borrowing an average of $513,208.
- [Annual rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-annual-milestone/): Over the 12 months to September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 33,485 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $19.61B in lending (up from 31,589 loans a year earlier)—including 15,743 buyers (47.0%) who bought with under a 20% deposit.
- [First-home buyer share of all bank low-deposit (>80% LVR) lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-bank-lvr-priority/): When New Zealand banks approve low-deposit mortgages (&gt;80% LVR), most of their allowance goes to first-home buyers. In September 2026, 67.2% of all low-deposit mortgage dollars ($850m of $1.26B) and 62.0% of low-deposit loans (1,342 of 2,165) went directly to first-home buyers.
- [Approved first-home buyer gross income — New Zealand vs Auckland (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-income-akl-vs-nz/): Because most first-home applications combine two incomes, approved first-home buyers in September 2026 averaged $144,232 in combined pre-tax income nationwide—though single-income buyers regularly qualify using regional price points, boarder income, or Kāinga Ora support.
- [First-home buyer average mortgage size by deposit tier (<20% vs 20%+ deposit) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-loan-size-gap/): First-home buyers with under a 20% deposit actually take out larger mortgages on average ($633,383) than buyers with a 20%+ deposit ($513,208)—a $120,175 difference in September 2026, as higher-earning couples often use a 10%–15% deposit to buy sooner rather than renting for extra years to save 20%.
- [First-home buyers with less than 20% deposit (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-low-deposit/): Buying a first home without a full 20% deposit is more common than many buyers expect. In September 2026, just over half of all first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (50.3%—1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) went to buyers with under a 20% deposit, up from 46.0% a year earlier.
- [Regional KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal averages across New Zealand (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-regional-kiwisaver/): Pooling two KiwiSaver accounts is how most Kiwi couples build their deposit—over the year to June 2026, 50,330 first-home buyers withdrew $2.27B from KiwiSaver, averaging $45,005 per person nationwide (~$90,000 per couple), led by Wellington ($50,364/person) and Auckland ($47,630/person).
- [First-home buyer share of total New Zealand mortgage lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-share/): First-home buyers continue to make up an active slice of the New Zealand market—in September 2026, banks approved 2,667 first-home mortgages (20.3% of all new mortgage lending, up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $574k.
- [First-home buyers vs property investors monthly lending comparison (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-vs-investors/): First-home buyers are out-borrowing property investors across New Zealand. In September 2026, banks approved $1.53B (20.3% of lending) for first-home buyers compared with $1.33B (17.7%) for property investors—putting first-home buyers $195m ahead.
- [Interest-only share of new investor vs owner-occupier mortgages (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/interest-only/): Loan structures look quite different between rental properties and family homes in the Reserve Bank figures—in September 2026, 31.5% of new investor lending was set up on interest-only terms (including revolving credit), compared with 13.7% for owner-occupiers.
- [Property investor equity tier breakdown (40%+, 30%–40%, and <30% equity) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-equity-tiers/): You don't need 40% equity locked up to buy an investment property. In September 2026, 43.8% of approved NZ property investors had 40%+ equity—while 36.4% bought in the 30%–40% equity band and 19.8% (527 loans, or $337m) were approved with under 30% equity.
- [Property investor loans approved with under 20% deposit (>80% LVR) & 20%–30% deposit (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-low-deposit/): Even for property investors, low-deposit approvals happen every month through new-build exemptions and bank speed limits. In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 52 investor mortgages ($36m, or 1.9% of investors) with strictly under a 20% deposit (&gt;80% LVR)—up from 34 loans ($23m) a year earlier (and 508 loans / $328m over the past 12 months)—plus another 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 20%–30% deposit tier (70%–80% LVR) where standard 20%-deposit new-build investment loans sit.
- [Property investors approved with under a 30% deposit (>70% LVR new-build & speed-limit tier) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-new-build-lvr/): Because brand-new builds are exempt from Reserve Bank LVR restrictions, nearly one in five property investors buys with less than the standard 30% existing-property deposit. In September 2026, 527 investor loans ($337m, or 19.8% of investor approvals) were approved with under a 30% deposit (&gt;70% LVR)—comprising 475 loans ($301m) in the 20%–30% deposit band (which includes 20%-deposit new builds) and 52 loans ($36m) with under a 20% deposit (&gt;80% LVR).
- [Investor vs owner-occupier interest-only mortgage share (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-vs-owner-io/): Loan structures look quite different between rental properties and family homes in the Reserve Bank figures—in September 2026, 31.5% of new investor lending was set up on interest-only terms (including revolving credit), compared with 13.7% for owner-occupiers.
- [Property investor share of new New Zealand mortgage lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investors/): First-home buyers are currently borrowing more overall than property investors—in September 2026, investors made up 17.7% of new mortgage lending ($1.33B, down from 21.2% a year earlier), compared with 20.3% for first-home buyers.
- [Active KiwiSaver provider switching volume (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-active-switchers/): Reviewing and changing KiwiSaver providers happens more regularly than many members realise—over the year to June 2026, 198,897 New Zealanders moved their balance to a new scheme, averaging 16,575 switches every month.
- [Monthly KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal count, value & average per buyer (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-first-home/): For many buyers, KiwiSaver does much of the heavy lifting toward a first deposit—in September 2026, 4,250 members withdrew a combined $195.7m to put toward a first home—averaging ~$46k per withdrawing member, or roughly $73k of KiwiSaver funds per approved first-home mortgage.
- [Annual and monthly KiwiSaver scheme transfers (members switching providers) (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-switches/): Reviewing and changing KiwiSaver providers happens more regularly than many members realise—over the year to June 2026, 198,897 New Zealanders moved their balance to a new scheme, averaging 16,575 switches every month.
- [Existing owner-occupiers approved with under 20% equity (>80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/mover-low-equity/): Low-deposit lending isn't restricted to first-home buyers. In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 769 mortgages ($378m) for existing owner-occupiers moving or borrowing with under 20% equity (&gt;80% LVR)—accounting for 5.1% of existing homeowner approvals, up from 3.3% a year earlier.
- [Annual new residential dwellings consented in New Zealand (Year ended September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/new-builds-annual/): New-build supply across New Zealand has been gathering pace, with 41,091 new homes consented in the year to September 2026 (up 18.0% on the previous year, including 3,570 dwellings consented in September 2026).
- [Existing owner-occupiers approved with 20% or more equity (<=80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/owner-equity-buffer/): Most existing Kiwi homeowners hold more usable equity than they realise. In September 2026, 94.9% of existing owner-occupier mortgages approved across New Zealand (14,327 of 15,096 loans, or $4.16B) had at least 20% equity, carrying an average loan size of $290,082.
- [Monthly mortgage refinancing ( borrowers switching bank providers) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/refinance/): Moving banks is a regular part of the New Zealand mortgage market rather than a rare step—in September 2026 alone, 2,772 borrowers switched mortgage providers, moving $1.73B in loans (23.0% of all new lending, at an average loan size of $624k).
- [New Zealand national and regional median weekly private rent (August 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/rent-yield-pulse/): Private weekly rents across New Zealand have been relatively steady over the past year—the national median sat at $595/wk in August 2026 (up 0.8% on a year earlier), with regional medians at $650/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $550/wk in Canterbury.
- [Monthly newly lodged and active private rental bonds in New Zealand (August 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/rental-bonds-supply/): Thousands of New Zealand households sign new leases every month—Tenancy Services logged 13,062 newly lodged private rental bonds in August 2026, across a nationwide pool of 522,942 active private tenancies.
- [Weighted-average settled 1-year and 2-year fixed mortgage interest rates (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/settled-rates/): Advertised bank rates only tell half the story—across all new fixed mortgages actually settled in September 2026, New Zealand borrowers locked in a weighted-average rate of 4.82% for one year and 5.09% for two years.
- [New Zealand median student loan balance (June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/student-loan-servicing/): Student debt is a familiar line item on home loan applications—across Inland Revenue's June 2026 figures, the median NZ student loan balance sat at $18,301 (up 4.5% on a year earlier), where compulsory PAYE deductions factor into how banks test monthly servicing.
- [Monthly mortgage top-ups on existing properties (borrower share & average top-up) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/top-ups/): Many Kiwi homeowners tap into existing equity for renovations or upgrades rather than moving house—in September 2026, 9,639 borrowers topped up an existing mortgage, making up 46.4% of all mortgage approvals by count (average top-up: $100k).
- [Multi-unit and townhouse share of new residential building consents (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/townhouse-share/): Townhouses and multi-unit developments now make up more than half of new residential consents—accounting for 51.5% (1,837 of 3,570 homes) consented in September 2026, including 1,305 townhouses, flats, and units.
